sourcedFrom: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: Faxon's own operator-level strip for the ARAK-21 upper, in Faxon's order and no further. The ARAK-21 is a gas-piston upper that carries its own recoil spring assembly at the rear of the upper receiver, so the AR-15 lower's buffer and buffer spring play no part in it and are not touched here. The bolt carrier and the gas piston are one part. The lower receiver the upper sits on is not covered by this book. Faxon warns that disassembly beyond its manual voids the warranty.

steps.title: Muzzle safe, safety on SAFE, magazine out
steps.action: Point the rifle in a safe direction and keep it there. Rotate the safety lever on the lower to SAFE, then take the magazine out of the magazine well.
steps.prose: The magazine comes out before the action is worked, so pulling the charging handle next cannot feed a fresh round into the chamber. The safety lever and magazine catch belong to the AR-15 lower the upper is mounted on.
steps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 4. Operation — 2. Clearing the ARAK-21, steps a–c, p.10

steps.title: Charging handle to the rear, bolt locked on the bolt stop
steps.action: Pull the charging handle fully to the rear and lock the bolt back on the bolt stop. Watch the ejection port for anything thrown out as the bolt comes back.
steps.prose: The ARAK-21's charging handle sits on the side of the upper, not at the rear like an AR-15's, and it can be set up on either side. With the bolt held open on the stop the chamber is in view for the next step.
steps.quote: Pull the charging handle to the rear and lock in place with the bolt stop.
steps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 4. Operation — 2. Clearing the ARAK-21, step d, p.10

steps.title: Look into the chamber
steps.action: Look into the chamber through the ejection port and confirm there is no live round and no empty case in it, and none in the magazine well.
steps.prose: Only an empty chamber, seen with your own eyes, ends the clearing. Faxon also warns never to look down the muzzle to inspect the bore; the bore is checked from the rear of the receiver once the bolt assembly is out.
steps.quote: Visually inspect the chamber for empty casings or live rounds.
steps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 4. Operation — 2. Clearing the ARAK-21, step e, p.10

steps.title: Bolt carrier and charging handle forward
steps.action: With the rifle cleared, let the bolt carrier and the charging handle go back to their forward position.
steps.prose: Faxon starts the strip with the carrier forward, not locked back; the recoil spring guide comes out first, and that is done with the carrier home.
steps.quote: Return bolt carrier (4) and charging handle (1) to the forward position.
steps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 5. Disassembly — Basic Field Stripping, step b, p.16

steps.title: Rear takedown pin pushed, upper and lower opened
steps.action: Push the rear takedown pin on the lower and hinge the upper and lower receivers open on the front pin.
steps.prose: The recoil spring guide and the bolt carrier come out of the back of the upper receiver, so the back of the upper has to be clear of the lower. Faxon's field-strip list does not print this line; its operation section opens the receivers this way to take the recoil spring and bolt assembly out, quoted here.
steps.quote: To safely visually inspect the bore, push the rear takedown pin and open the upper and lower receiver. Remove the recoil spring and bolt assembly and look from the rear of the receiver down the barrel.
steps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 4. Operation, p.8

steps.title: Recoil spring guide retainer pin out
steps.action: Push the recoil spring guide retainer pin out of the upper receiver.
steps.prose: This cross pin is all that holds the recoil spring guide in the upper. The guide is under spring pressure behind it, so keep a hand at the rear of the upper as the pin comes out, and put the pin straight in a tray.
steps.quote: Push out recoil spring guide retainer pin (2).
steps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 5. Disassembly — Basic Field Stripping, step c, p.16

steps.title: Recoil spring guide in, down and out the back
steps.action: Press the recoil spring guide about half an inch into the upper, rotate it slightly downward, and take it out of the back of the upper receiver.
steps.prose: The guide has to be pressed in against its spring before it will turn; trying to rotate it without pressing it in only fights the spring. Faxon makes two recoil spring assemblies: the silver one is for .223/5.56 and 7.62x39, the shorter yellow one for .300 BLK only, so note which one came out.
steps.quote: Press the recoil spring guide (3) in 1/2", rotate downward slightly, and remove out the back of the upper receiver.
steps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 5. Disassembly — Basic Field Stripping, step d, p.16

steps.title: Charging handle back, bolt carrier assembly out
steps.action: Pull the charging handle rearward and take the bolt carrier assembly out of the upper.
steps.prose: On the ARAK-21 the gas piston is part of the bolt carrier, so the piston comes out with the carrier. Draw it out straight so the piston end does not drag through the receiver.
steps.quote: Pull charging handle (1) rearward and remove the bolt carrier assembly (4).
steps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 5. Disassembly — Basic Field Stripping, step e, p.16

steps.title: Gas adjuster to Position 1, pulled out
steps.action: Rotate the gas adjuster at the front of the upper to Position 1, the insert/remove position with the indicator pointing straight up, and pull it out of the gas block.
steps.prose: Position 1 is the only position the adjuster comes out in. Faxon warns that the rifle must never be fired with the adjuster left in that position: the adjuster is propelled downrange. Each caliber has its own adjuster, engraved with its caliber.
steps.quote: Rotate the gas adjuster (5) to Position 1 and pull to remove.
steps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 5. Disassembly — Basic Field Stripping, step f, p.16

steps.title: Field strip complete — Faxon's operator level
steps.action: You now have the upper receiver with its barrel, the recoil spring guide and its retainer pin, the bolt carrier assembly with the gas piston, and the gas adjuster. Taking the bolt out of the carrier, the charging handle out of the upper, and the barrel assembly out of the upper are published in the same section and are the deep clean.
steps.prose: Faxon draws the line in its own words: its manual sets the limit of owner disassembly, and anything past it voids the warranty.
steps.quote: Disassembly beyond the level outlined in this manual will void the warranty and can potentially cause damage or injury.
steps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 5. Disassembly, notice, p.16

steps.title: Bore from the breech end with the right bronze brush
steps.action: Run the cleaning rod through the barrel from the breech end, with a bronze bore brush sized to the barrel: .22 caliber for a 5.56mm/.223 barrel, .30 caliber for a .30 caliber barrel. Then swab the bore and the chamber clean.
steps.prose: Going in from the breech keeps the rod off the rifling at the muzzle, which is why Faxon recommends it. Use a one-piece rod: Faxon warns that multi-section steel military rods can damage the bore.
steps.quote: For 5.56mm/.223 caliber barrels, use a .22 caliber bronze bore brush.
steps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 7. Cleaning — Cleaning Supplies, p.25

steps.title: Gas cylinder with the .38 brush, piston end, gas adjuster
steps.action: Brush out the gas cylinder with a .38 caliber bore brush, whichever barrel is fitted. Clean the gas piston end on the bolt carrier and the gas adjuster.
steps.prose: The gas piston keeps most of the fouling forward, in the gas cylinder, on the piston end and in the adjuster's ports, not in the bolt. A fouled gas port is one of Faxon's named causes of the rifle failing to cycle.
steps.quote: Both caliber barrel assemblies use a .38 caliber bore brush to clean the gas cylinder.
steps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 7. Cleaning — Cleaning Supplies, p.25

steps.title: Bolt face kept free of brass and primer deposits
steps.action: Clean the bolt face of brass, powder fouling and primer sealant. Wipe the bolt carrier and check the firing pin hole and the extractor groove are clean.
steps.prose: Because the gas does not blow back into the bolt, its insides foul far less than an AR-15's and need cleaning less often, but the bolt face does not get that pass. A dirty firing pin hole and fouling in the extractor groove are among Faxon's named causes of failures to fire and to extract.
steps.quote: The bolt face still needs regular cleaning to keep it free of brass and primer sealing deposits.
steps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 5. Disassembly — 2. Bolt Disassembly, note, p.17

deepSteps.title: Firing pin out — gate retainer carrier
deepSteps.action: If your carrier has the gate-type firing pin retainer: press the firing pin release lever down, pull the firing pin out of the bolt carrier, and take out the firing pin buffer spring.
deepSteps.prose: Faxon builds the carrier two ways; this step is the gate retainer type, the next the cross pin type. Keep the buffer spring: it is there to lessen the risk of slam-fire, and Faxon wants it back in for 5.56 and .300 BLK.
deepSteps.quote: Press firing pin release lever (1) down.
deepSteps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 5. Disassembly — 2. Bolt Disassembly (On Gate Retainer Type Bolt Carrier), steps a–c, p.17

deepSteps.title: Firing pin out — cross pin carrier
deepSteps.action: If your carrier has the cross pin firing pin retainer instead: press the retainer cross pin out of the bolt carrier, then pull the firing pin out of the carrier.
deepSteps.prose: The cross pin is small and easy to lose, so put it straight in a tray with the firing pin.
deepSteps.quote: Press Firing Pin Retainer (5) Cross Pin out of bolt carrier.
deepSteps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 5. Disassembly — 2. Bolt Disassembly (On Cross Pin Type Bolt Carrier), steps a–b, p.18

deepSteps.title: Bolt cam out — note its large radius corner
deepSteps.action: Take the bolt cam out of the carrier, noting which way its large radius corner faces.
deepSteps.prose: The cam goes back in only one way round, and the large radius corner is how you tell. Look before it comes out, not after.
deepSteps.quote: Remove bolt cam (3), noting the orientation of the large radius corner
deepSteps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 5. Disassembly — 2. Bolt Disassembly, step d, p.17

deepSteps.title: Bolt out of the front of the carrier
deepSteps.action: With the cam out, pull the bolt out from the front of the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.prose: The bolt leaves forward, not out the back. The ARAK-21's bolt looks like an AR-15 bolt but Faxon says none of the parts interchange.
deepSteps.quote: Pull bolt (4) out from the front of the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 5. Disassembly — 2. Bolt Disassembly, step e, p.17

deepSteps.title: Extractor pin out, extractor and spring off — ejectors stay in
deepSteps.action: Push the extractor pin out of the bolt and take off the extractor and the extractor spring. Leave the ejectors and their pin alone.
deepSteps.prose: Faxon prints this step in the cross pin carrier's list; the bolt itself is the same part in both carrier types in Faxon's parts lists. On reassembly Faxon calls it critical to orient the extractor so the case ejects out of the port. This is the end of the bolt: Faxon says no further disassembly is needed.
deepSteps.quote: Push out extractor pin (5) and remove extractor (6) and extractor spring (7).
deepSteps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 5. Disassembly — 2. Bolt Disassembly, step e, p.18
deepSteps.warn: The dual ejectors are under strong spring tension.

deepSteps.title: Charging handle off the upper
deepSteps.action: With the handle almost closed, push it rearward against its spring so the detent spring compresses toward the rear. Then pull or push the tip of the handle forward toward the receiver, and take the handle away from the upper.
deepSteps.prose: The handle is held by a spring-loaded detent; pushing it rearward first is what frees the tip to swing. Do not force the handle sideways against the detent.
deepSteps.quote: Then pull or push the tip of the handle forward towards the receiver. You can now push or pull the handle away from the upper receiver.
deepSteps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 5. Disassembly — 3. Charging Handle, step a, p.20

deepSteps.title: Charger spring out of its track, charging block out
deepSteps.action: Push the charger spring guide forward and rotate the spring up and out of its track. Then pull the charging block back and lift it out of the receiver where its tabs line up with the openings machined in the upper.
deepSteps.prose: The block lifts out only where its tabs meet the openings in the receiver; it does not come out anywhere else along the track. Faxon stops here: the return spring and detent spring stay as they are.
deepSteps.quote: Push charger spring guide forward (1). Rotate spring up and out of track.
deepSteps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 5. Disassembly — 3. Charging Handle, steps b–c, p.20
deepSteps.warn: Further disassembly of the return spring or detent spring is not required or recommended.

deepSteps.title: Lower forearm off — six allen screws
deepSteps.action: Lay the upper upside down on the bench. Loosen the six allen screws that hold the lower forearm to the upper receiver, and lift the forearm straight up and off.
deepSteps.prose: Lift straight up: the forearm locates on four stainless alignment pins. The screws thread into stainless heli-coils in the receiver, and Faxon says not to try to remove those coils.
deepSteps.quote: Loosen six allen screws (1) holding the lower forearm (2) to the upper receiver (3) and remove the lower forearm (2) by lifting straight up.
deepSteps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 5. Disassembly — Removing/Changing Barrel Assembly Unit (BAU), step a, p.21

deepSteps.title: Barrel assembly forward and out
deepSteps.action: Slide the barrel assembly forward, then lift it out of the upper receiver.
deepSteps.prose: The barrel assembly unit comes out whole, with its trunnion, gas block and gas tube. Leave the bolt rails and recoil lug in the receiver: Faxon says removing them voids the warranty and can affect accuracy and reliability. Use only the barrels shipped with this upper.
deepSteps.quote: To remove the barrel assembly (4), slide the barrel assembly forward and then out of the upper receiver (3).
deepSteps.cite: ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual — ARAK-21 Upper Assembly Operator Safety and Instruction Manual (undated; file ARAK-21-Manual (1).pdf) — 5. Disassembly — Removing/Changing Barrel Assembly Unit, step b, p.22
deepSteps.warn: Have cartridge headspace checked by a qualified gunsmith if barrels become mixed up.

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHAMBER
tasks: Bronze bore brush sized to the barrel: .22 caliber for 5.56mm/.223, .30 caliber for a .30 caliber barrel
Cleaning rod pushed through from the breech end, never from the muzzle
Do not use multi-section steel cleaning rods like those in military kits
Bore swabbed with a swab holder until clean

cleaning.name: GAS SYSTEM
tasks: .38 caliber bore brush through the gas cylinder (every caliber)
Gas piston end on the bolt carrier cleaned
Gas adjuster cleaned; check its caliber engraving matches the barrel
Barrel and upper receiver mating surfaces clean before the barrel goes back in

cleaning.name: BOLT CARRIER GROUP
tasks: Bolt face cleaned of brass, powder fouling and primer sealant
Ejectors free and moving — never removed by the owner
Firing pin buffer spring present for 5.56 and .300 BLK

cleaning.name: FINISH
tasks: ⛔ Never use steel wire brushes, oven cleaning or ultrasonic baths — Faxon says they may damage the finish and void the warranty

reassembly: Barrel assembly laid into the upper receiver and slid rearward, taking care to align the slots. Mating surfaces on the barrel and upper receiver clean first.
Lower forearm positioned on the receiver so the alignment pins slip into place; six allen screws tightened. Do not over-tighten: Faxon recommends 30 in-lbs.
Charging block into the receiver where its tabs meet the machined openings, pushed forward; charger spring rotated back into its track; charging handle refitted on the side you use.

Extractor and extractor spring onto the bolt, extractor pin pushed in. Faxon calls it critical to orient the extractor so the spent case ejects out of the port; the same bolt serves right- and left-hand uppers.
Bolt into the front of the bolt carrier; bolt cam in with its large radius corner the way it came out.

Firing pin buffer spring into the firing pin hole until it seats in the bottom of the counter-bore (5.56 and .300 BLK), then the firing pin, then the retainer: gate lever closed or the cross pin pressed back in.

Gas adjuster inserted in Position 1, then rotated to a firing position. The lines on the adjuster must line up with the lines on the gas block; you should feel the detent seat. Never fire it in Position 1.
Bolt carrier assembly into the upper with the charging handle; carrier forward.

Recoil spring guide in at the back of the upper, pressed in and rotated into place, and the retainer pin pushed back in. Silver spring for 5.56/.223 and 7.62x39; the shorter yellow spring for .300 BLK only.
Upper and lower closed together and the rear takedown pin pushed closed.
fncheck: Faxon's book prints no dry function check for the upper. With the rifle unloaded: confirm the gas adjuster is NOT in Position 1 (indicator straight up) and that its lines meet the gas block lines with the detent seated. Insert an empty magazine and pull the charging handle back; the bolt should lock to the rear on the bolt stop. Faxon's own first live check is the gas setting: start at Position 2 (Low Gas) with one round in the magazine, fire it into the backstop, and the bolt carrier should lock open on the bolt stop; if it does not, go up one position and repeat. Shoot on the lowest setting that cycles reliably.
